Expected behaviour (code-backed): The installed `radon` command calls `radon.main`, then dispatches to the selected subcommand.
`python -m radon ...` imports and calls the same main entrypoint.
When no arguments are supplied, `-h` is appended before command parsing.
The command program is initialized with package version 6.0.1 and exposes the framework's version option.
Exceptions escaping command dispatch are caught and emitted with a colored `ERROR:` prefix.
Every command requires one or more positional paths; each path is walked or read as appropriate.
If the path set is only `-`, Radon reads `sys.stdin` and yields the result under filename `-`.
Directory trees are traversed with `os.walk`; eligible files are yielded for analysis.
Files ending in `.py` are accepted as Python source.
A non-`.py` file is accepted when its first line starts with `#!` and contains `python`.
A comma-separated `--exclude` string is split into glob patterns and matched against full file paths.
A comma-separated `--ignore` string filters directory names/paths using glob matching before descent.
The implicit ignore pattern `.*` is always included; hidden files are also suppressed during directory traversal.
`RADONFILESENCODING` selects the encoding used to open source files; Python 3 defaults to UTF-8 and PyPy uses its native path.
If `RADONCFG` names an existing file, it is read before the conventional local files.
An existing `radon.cfg` in the working directory is read into section `[radon]`.
The `[tool.radon]` table is loaded through `tomllib`/`tomli` and merged into the config parser.
`setup.cfg` is read after local/TOML configuration.
`~/.radon.cfg` is read after project-local configuration.
Configured integers use `getint`, booleans use `getboolean`, and other values use string retrieval; missing keys retain command defaults.
A `TOMLDecodeError` is re-raised; missing files/tables and other lookup failures yield no TOML defaults.
`-O/--output-file` opens the path in text write mode; otherwise output goes to stdout.
Exceptions raised while parsing a file are captured as `{error: message}` results and emitted alongside other files.
The first iteration caches `(filename, result)` tuples; later `results` access returns the cached list.
`COLOR=yes` forces color, `COLOR=auto` enables it only for a TTY, and other values disable it; missing colorama falls back to empty codes.
With `nbformat` installed, `.ipynb` is recognized; analysis occurs only when `--include-ipynb` is enabled.
Code-cell sources are concatenated with newlines and analyzed as a single document; markdown and other cells are ignored.
With `--ipynb-cells`, each code cell is additionally analyzed and keyed as `file.ipynb:[zero_based_index]`.
Lines whose first character is `%` are removed before analysis; indented or other magic forms are not specially stripped.
Source is parsed to AST and returns block objects containing names, locations, nesting context, and complexity.
Scores 1–5=A, 6–10=B, 11–20=C, 21–30=D, 31–40=E, and 41+=F; negative scores raise `ValueError`.
Each `if`, `elif` AST node, and ternary `if` expression adds one; `else` adds none by itself.
A BoolOp adds `number of values - 1`, so each additional `and`/`or` operand adds a decision.
A try adds one per exception handler plus one when a try-`else` exists; `finally` adds no decision.
Each `for`, `while`, or `async for` adds one; a loop `else` adds one more.
Every comprehension generator adds one, plus one for each attached `if` filter; nested generators accumulate.
A `match` adds one per case except a wildcard `_` fallback; an all-wildcard match adds zero.
Each `assert` adds one unless `no_assert=True` / `--no-assert` is used.
`with` and `async with` add no complexity in the current visitor.
A lambda does not create a separate complexity block; decisions inside its expression (such as a ternary) are still visited.
`AsyncFunctionDef` delegates to the standard function visitor.
A class stores real body complexity; displayed class complexity is the integer average over methods, rounded by the implementation's method-count rule.
Closures are attached to their parent function and excluded from its direct body-complexity accumulation; `show_closures` can promote them to named top-level results.
Inner classes are retained on the parent class and can be flattened with qualified names by `add_inner_blocks`.
`--min` and `--max` are uppercased; only blocks with ranks lexically between those letters are exported/displayed.
`-s/--show-complexity` appends `(<score>)` to each terminal block line.
`--order SCORE` sorts complexity descending and is the fallback for unknown order values.
`--order LINES` sorts by starting line number ascending.
`--order ALPHA` sorts block names ascending.
`-a/--average` reports analyzed block count and mean score using only blocks surviving rank filtering.
`--total-average` includes every analyzed block in the average even if the block is not displayed.
`--json` returns a filename-keyed object; blocks include type, rank, complexity, location and nested method/closure data, filtered by rank.
`--xml` emits `<ccm><metric>` elements with complexity, qualified unit, classification, file, and start/end lines.
`--md` emits a table containing filename, qualified name, type letter, start/end line, complexity, and classification.
`--codeclimate` emits null-delimited JSON issue strings only when remediation points exceed zero; parse errors become Bug Risk issues.
`loc` equals SLOC + blank + multiline-string lines + single-comment/docstring-only lines.
`lloc` counts logical statements, including multiple semicolon-separated statements and same-line suite statements after a colon.
Nonblank parsed lines not classified as standalone comments/docstrings contribute to `sloc`.
Every tokenizer COMMENT token contributes to `comments`, including comments appearing after code.
A line consisting of a COMMENT token, or a one-line standalone STRING/docstring, contributes to `single_comments`.
Nonblank lines belonging to a standalone multiline STRING contribute to `multi`; blank lines inside it contribute to `blank`.
Empty stripped physical lines contribute to `blank`, including empty lines inside multiline strings.
Terminal output lists seven metrics plus C/LOC, C/SLOC and (comments+multi)/LOC percentages, protecting division by zero.
`-s/--summary` sums each raw metric and prints aggregate comment ratios after per-file output.
`--json` returns filename-keyed raw metric dictionaries; the optional terminal summary is not included.
Raw XML export raises `NotImplementedError`; no CLI flag exposes it.
Binary, unary, boolean, augmented-assignment, and comparison nodes update total/distinct operator and operand sets.
Reports include h1, h2, N1, N2, vocabulary, length, calculated length, volume, difficulty, effort, estimated time, and estimated bugs; zero vocabularies avoid log/division errors.
`h_visit` returns a `Halstead` tuple whose `total` report aggregates scanned module and function expressions.
The result includes `(function_name, report)` pairs for top-level functions; nested functions are not tracked as separate reports.
Async function definitions delegate to the normal Halstead function visitor.
Without `--functions`, each filename is followed by all 12 fields from its total report.
`-f/--functions` prints each top-level function and its 12 metrics instead of the whole-file total.
`--json` serializes each file with `total` and a name-keyed `functions` object, each containing all report fields.
The CLI explicitly passes XML and Markdown as false and HCHarvester supplies neither specialized exporter.
MI combines Halstead volume, cyclomatic complexity, logical lines of code (LLOC), and comment percentage, then normalizes and clamps the result to 0–100.
If Halstead volume or SLOC is nonpositive, MI returns 100.0 without logarithms.
`mi_parameters(..., count_multi=True)` adds `raw.multi` to comment lines; false counts only COMMENT tokens.
Scores >19 rank A; >9 and <=19 rank B; <=9 rank C.
`--min` and `--max` are uppercased; errors are preserved and non-error results are retained when rank is in range.
`-s/--show` appends the MI rounded to two decimal places after the rank.
`--sort` orders filtered results by numeric MI ascending; otherwise discovery order is retained.
`--json` serializes filtered results as `{filename: {mi, rank}}`, preserving error objects.
MI XML export raises `NotImplementedError`; no CLI flag exposes it.
`code2ast(source)` returns `ast.parse(source)` without preprocessing or compatibility conversion.
`CodeVisitor.from_code` parses source and delegates to `from_ast` with caller options.
`CodeVisitor.from_ast` constructs the visitor, visits the supplied node, and returns the populated visitor.
`average_complexity` returns the arithmetic mean or 0 for an empty list.
`sorted_results` returns a new list sorted using SCORE, LINES, ALPHA, or a caller-supplied key.
`analyze` returns a `Module` namedtuple with loc, lloc, sloc, comments, multi, blank, and single_comments.
Function and Class namedtuples expose letter/fullname/string forms, locations, nesting data, and computed complexity semantics.
The `R70` extension entrypoint loads `Flake8Checker`; violations use code R701.
`--radon-max-cc` sets an integer threshold; blocks strictly greater emit `(line, column, R701 message, checker type)`.
`--radon-no-assert` disables assert complexity; if it is the only Radon option, the checker activates with default max CC 10.
`--radon-show-closures` flattens closures and inner classes before applying the threshold.
`/config.json` config.threshold is lowercased and passed to `radon cc -n<threshold> --codeclimate`; default is B.
Config value 2 selects `radon2`; 3 retains `radon3`; any other nonempty value exits with a validation message.
Config `encoding` is assigned to `RADONFILESENCODING` before invoking Radon.
Configured include paths are shell-quoted and retained only when they are directories or end in `.py`; the default is current directory.
If no eligible include paths remain, the runner prints `Empty workspace; skipping...` and does not invoke Radon.
MD5 is computed from path, the literal `Complexity`, and issue identity parts (block type/name or error).
Points are zero at/below the grade's maximum; above it they are 1,000,000 + 100,000 per excess point. Unknown/A thresholds fall back to max 5.
